children: Gold declines in Asian trade. Thursday's U.S. producer price index release and Friday's consumer-price index data are likely to set the tone around rate-hike expectations for the Sept. 15-16 Federal Reserve meeting, says Critical Metals' Tony Sage in commentary. A hawkish reading of the two data releases could lift bond yields and weigh on gold's gains, he says, while softer inflation could lead to rate-hike bets being pared back. "Traders will also watch developments in the Middle East and oil prices, which remain a source of risk," he says. A higher interest rate environment typically weighs on nonyielding assets such as gold. Spot gold eases 0.2% to $4,346.86 a troy ounce. (megan.cheah@wsj.com)
